candidates.title: Engineered microbes for planetary-scale terraforming
candidates.shift: Bio-engineered bacteria being developed to alter soil/atmosphere at scale, adjacent to emerging bio-based construction and remediation materials (living concrete, bioremediation agents).
candidates.ai_read: Tentative and strange off-map wildcard: could eventually seed construction inputs or brownfield-to-retail site remediation if bio-manufacturing scales, though today it's pure climate-science research.
candidates.evidence: Noema feature describes a lab growing mutant bacteria intended to help terraform Earth.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from purely chemical/mechanical environmental remediation to engineered biological agents; could eventually touch construction material inputs and contaminated-site retail redevelopment.
candidates.author: Matthew Ponsford

candidates.title: Kiosk robots edge toward retail-floor wayfinding
candidates.shift: Robotic wayfinding/reception assistants being researched for large institutional campuses (hospitals, colleges), conceptually transferable to big-box stores and malls.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: an academic prototype, but it signals a category — autonomous in-store concierge — that doesn't yet have a retail deployment standard.
candidates.evidence: Paper describes a kiosk robot addressing navigation and facility-info gaps at institutional campuses.
candidates.source: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from static signage to autonomous wayfinding agents; if applied to retail could reshape front-of-store greeting and customer-service staffing functions.
candidates.author: Yasmeen Begum D, Yuvasree P, Swetha Fastyna A
